question: Harmonium player, Tulsidas Borkar, was awarded with the ________ in 2016.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Shri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Tulsidas Borkar was a renowned harmonium player known for his contributions to Indian classical music.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016 for his exceptional contribution to the field of arts.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished service in various disciplines.

• His mastery and innovative techniques in harmonium playing earned him this prestigious recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Padma Awards**

• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.

• Instituted in 1954, the awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

• The Padma Vibhushan is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service; the Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of high order; and the Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field.

• The awards seek to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved.

• **Harmonium**

• The harmonium is a free-reed organ that generates sound as air flows past a vibrating piece of thin metal in a frame.

• It is widely used in Indian classical music and is a significant instrument in the genres of Khayal, Thumri, and Bhajan.

• The instrument has keys like a piano and is played by hand, with air being pumped through bellows operated by hand or foot.

• Harmonium players like Tulsidas Borkar have greatly contributed to its popularity and development in Indian music.

• **Indian Classical Music**

• Indian classical music is a genre of South Asian music, rooted in ancient traditions and scriptures.

• It has two major traditions: the North Indian Hindustani classical music and the South Indian Carnatic music.

• Classical music in India is characterized by its complex rhythms, intricate melodies, and a wide range of instruments including the sitar, tabla, and harmonium.

• It is known for its improvisational nature and its deep spiritual and cultural significance.
